claim: This type is a chain of four fixed filter sections and an output gain: a low shelf, two peaking sections that share one law, a high shelf. The low shelf is one pole and one zero. Each parameter byte selects from a short table rather than driving a formula -- a gain answers over twenty-five values and sticks at both ends, a corner has two states, a width has five entries and returns the first for anything past them, a centre moves in equal steps of log frequency for every eighth value of its byte.
why_not_named: Naming it would add nothing the claim does not already say and would carry a topology this run did not test. The high shelf's order is open, and a name would close it by implication.

era_priors.claim: A parameter byte indexes a coefficient table rather than driving a formula.
era_priors.why: Computing a filter coefficient from a byte needs transcendental functions a fixed-point part of that period does not have, and a table of a few tens of entries costs it nothing.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: A parameter answered differently at every one of its 128 values with no repeats. Four of this type's eleven bytes repeat: the widths have five entries, the corners two, the centres one per eight values, and the gains one per value over a window of twenty-five.

era_priors.claim: The chain runs below the converter's rate, so its response ends at that rate's half.
era_priors.why: Effect processing shared a slower clock than the output in this generation of part.
era_priors.would_be_wrong_if: The unit answered above the half rate the model assumes. It does not: the output stands 31.9 dB over silence at 16 kHz, 16.3 at 17 and nothing at 18.

adds: The archive says what each byte did to each band. It does not say that those profiles are the response of a cascade of second-order sections, that the low shelf is one pole rather than two, or that the two mids are one law rather than two that happen to agree at the three settings both were asked at. Each of those is a structure fitted to the readings, and the fit is what this file holds.

alternatives.reading: The high shelf is one pole and one zero, as the low one is.

separated_by.observable: The high shelf's profile where it levels off.

predicts.first order: About 3.6 dB per octave through the corner.

separated_by.sensitivity_here: The slope is published at two resolutions and they agree for the low shelf (3.5 to 3.7) and disagree for the high one (7.1 against 9.8), which is what a profile still climbing at the edge of the set does.
separated_by.why_not_separable: The high shelf has not levelled off where the unit's own output ends. It is still climbing 4.2 dB per third octave at 16 kHz, and by 18 kHz there is no output to read. Separating the two orders needs the profile past its corner, and this unit cannot be made to put a signal there: the analogue input does not reach the insertion effects, so every excitation is one of its own voices. Nothing about the model decides this and no further reading of these takes will.

alternatives.reading: The low shelf is a second-order shelving section.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: Its residual leans across the bands of the low corner's record where the first-order one does not, and the low shelf's profile did settle inside the band set, so the lean is the model's and not the reading's. The two candidates that put a second-order section at the low end are the only two of the five that lean on a record whose profile the bands contained.

alternatives.reading: The width byte selects the Q values the manual prints against it.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: It leans on six of the fourteen records that carry an effect, against none for the measured widths, and its residual is the largest of the five candidates on every record. The printed figures are about twice the measured ones, which is the size of a bandwidth-convention difference, and the unit answers to the measured ones.

the_cut_that_is_not_the_boost.what: A peaking section's cut is not its boost inverted. Read at all twenty-five of one section's gain settings rather than at three, the mirrored pair at nine decibels comes back 0.46 dB apart at the widest width and 0.14 at the width one along, where three other pairs are inside a quarter of a decibel at both. Every model in this catalogue renders a peaking section whose cut is the exact mirror of its boost, so none of them has this.
the_cut_that_is_not_the_boost.not_on_the_shelves: The same asymmetry is absent from the shelf pair, whose cut is its boost negated to a median 0.02 dB over twenty-two bands on another type. So this is the peaking sections and not the chain.
the_cut_that_is_not_the_boost.why_it_is_here_and_not_in_the_gain_class: The byte is a decibel a step on both halves; what differs is what the section does with the number. That is this type's topology, and the gain class says so and hands it back.
the_cut_that_is_not_the_boost.what_would_settle_it: The same mirrored pairs at the three widths not yet asked, and on a centre away from the middle of the band set. Whether the asymmetry is a constant, a function of the width, or a rounding is not read yet, and the pairs that are inside a quarter of a decibel bound it to something small over most of the byte.

compared_against.generated_from: data/units/roland-sc8850-01/index.json, every efx-bands record filed under type 01 00 at the twelfth-octave resolution

excluded.why: The same takes read at the coarser set. Scoring both resolutions counts one measurement twice and weights the rows that have two records over the rows that have one.

stimulus: channel 2, program 126, note 60, velocity 100, held 8.0 s, captured 9.0 s
domain.outside: One byte at a time. No setting where two of the four sections are away from their centre together was asked, so the chain's sections are shown to be right one at a time and not shown to combine. Nothing above 16 kHz, where the unit's output ends. Nothing about phase: the phase records for this type exist and this run did not read them.

residual.unit: share of the span the effect commands in that record
residual.why: Of the 22 records that carry an effect, 2 have a residual that leans across their settings or their bands by more than the run's own floor: 01-00-07-the-entry-that-is-not-printed-in-twelfths.json, 01-00-0A-the-entry-that-is-not-printed-in-twelfths.json. The records whose residual leans and whose profile the band set did not contain are counted apart -- what leans there is the bound the model's corner was transcribed from and not the model, and the record says so itself.

breaks_down_at.why: Where a single setting's residual is more than half the span that record's own effect commands. Every one of them is a centre frequency record and every one is at the same place: the model's frequency table takes its third entry from the printed third octave and the unit does not put it there. That is the point the frequency class already carries as its own breakdown, arriving here because this chain reads the same table.
breaks_down_at.what_it_does_not_reach: The gain rows. Twenty-five settings of one peaking section's gain were added to this set and none of them leans under this reading, so what the chain has wrong is where a centre sits and not what a gain is worth.

gross.why: The median residual over the span the effect commands, taken as the worst of the records scored. A rejection bound and not a target: below it the residual is reported and never optimised, because no candidate is decided by it.

qualitative.why: Properties the unit's readings have that the model's readings must have too. No arithmetic over a residual rescues a model that cuts where the unit boosts.

power.why: The runner-up in the catalogue, scored on the same records, and whether it leans or contradicts a property where the winner does neither. The decoy is not chosen -- it is whichever candidate came second, so a strawman cannot be put up in its place. A class holding one candidate is a catalogue that is unfinished, which is a finding and not a pass.

records_the_run_did_not_reach.why: The profile had not levelled off where the band set ended, so the corner the model takes from this record is a lower bound. A residual leaning across the bands is that bound leaning. Answering it needs a stimulus that reaches further, not a different model.

The profile had not levelled off where the band set ended, so the corner the model takes from this record is a lower bound. A residual leaning across the bands is that bound leaning. Answering it needs a stimulus that reaches further, not a different model.

breakdown.why: A point worse than 0.5 of the span is a failure at that point rather than error at it. A residual that leans with the setting or with frequency is pointing at a structure the model does not have; one that does not is pointing at the room and the converters, and is not made smaller by anything this project can do.

refuted_by: A setting of any of the eleven bytes whose band profile the chain cannot produce at all -- a second peak, an asymmetric one, a corner that moves with the gain applied through it. Or a byte turning out to answer at values the tables here say are repeats: the widths at 5 and above, the centres between multiples of eight, the gains outside 52 to 76.
what_this_does_not_settle: Which of the two printed labels goes with which state of a corner byte. A label is not measurable.
The high shelf's order, and with it its asymptotic gain and its corner as a value rather than a bound.
Whether the sections combine as the chain says. Every reading was taken with one byte away from its centre.
Phase. The archive holds phase records for this type below 1 kHz and this run compared band energies only.
Whether the same eleven bytes behave this way on any other unit, or under the MSB 04 composite types that print the same rows.
